extra_misconceptions.fact: Decayed tooth structure loses mineral density, so X-rays pass through it more easily and create dark radiolucent shadows.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dental caries appear as bright white radiopaque spots on a standard bitewing dental X-ray.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Enamel covers only the anatomical crown above the gumline, while softer cementum covers the root surfaces anchored in bone.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Enamel covers the entire exterior of a molar from the chewing crown down to the root tip.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Nerves and blood vessels enter from the jawbone through the apical foramen at the very tip of each root canal.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Blood vessels and nerves enter a tooth through microscopic pores along the chewing surface.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The fibrous periodontal ligament suspends the root in its socket and absorbs chewing forces between cementum and alveolar bone.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Healthy tooth roots fuse directly to the surrounding jawbone without any soft tissue layer between them.

extra_socratic_questions: What visual contrast on a bitewing radiograph distinguishes healthy enamel from early interproximal decay?
Where do nerves and blood vessels enter a lower molar root to supply the internal pulp chamber?
Which anatomical surfaces of a lower molar trap bacterial plaque most readily between daily brushings?
Why does alveolar bone appear lighter on an X-ray than the periodontal ligament space around the root?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Oral bacteria in plaque ferment dietary sugars and excrete lactic acid, which then strips calcium and phosphate from enamel.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dietary sugar directly dissolves tooth enamel on contact during meals and sweet drinks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scrubbing or drying kills vital root cells; hold the tooth by the crown and store it in cold milk or saline until replanted.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A knocked-out permanent tooth should be scrubbed clean with soap and wrapped dry in a tissue.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Replanting a primary tooth can damage the permanent tooth bud developing directly underneath it inside the jawbone.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Knocked-out baby teeth should be pushed back into the gum socket immediately after an injury.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bleeding gums usually indicate gingivitis caused by plaque buildup, which requires gentle, consistent brushing and daily flossing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Bleeding gums during brushing mean you should stop flossing until the tissue heals completely.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to enamel mineral crystals when oral pH drops below 5.5 after a sugary snack?
Why is it dangerous to scrub the root surface of a knocked-out permanent tooth before replanting it?
Which preservation liquid keeps periodontal ligament cells alive longest if an avulsed tooth cannot be replanted?
What structural advantage does a custom-fitted vacuum mouth guard offer over a stock athletic mouth guard?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Disclosing dye temporarily colors invisible bacterial plaque biofilm so patients can see missed spots and brush them away.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Disclosing tablets permanently stain decayed enamel so the dentist knows where to drill.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A comprehensive exam checks gum pocket depths, jaw joint motion, bite alignment, and soft tissues for signs of oral pathology.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A routine dental checkup only inspects hard tooth crowns for cavities and ignores soft oral tissues.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Healthy gingival sulcus depths measure one to three millimeters, whereas depths over four millimeters signal gum detachment.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Periodontal probe depths of five to six millimeters indicate tight, healthy gum attachment around a tooth.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Professional scaling instruments fracture and remove hardened calculus deposits that cannot be brushed off at home.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Ultrasonic scalers and hand curettes remove only soft food debris that a regular toothbrush missed.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement confirms whether the gingival sulcus has deepened into a periodontal pocket during probing?
Which physical indicator does a disclosing tablet reveal on teeth that look clean to the naked eye?
Why does a dentist palpate the lymph nodes and inspect the tongue and cheeks during a routine checkup?
Under what condition does a dentist use an explorer tip gently rather than pressing hard into enamel pits?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Excess water weakens the hardened gypsum crystal lattice, while too little water makes the mix too thick to flow into details.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Guessing the water-to-powder ratio when mixing dental stone produces a stronger, faster-setting cast.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Stone must be flowed in small increments from one side on a dental vibrator so rising air bubbles escape ahead of the wave.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dumping all the stone into the impression mould at once prevents air pockets from forming on the cusps.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Frequent snacking or sipping sugary drinks keeps oral pH acidic for hours, preventing saliva from remineralizing enamel.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Total grams of sugar consumed in a day matter more for cavity risk than how often snacks are eaten.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An autoclave uses high-pressure saturated steam at elevated temperatures to kill all bacteria, viruses, and heat-resistant spores.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A dental autoclave sterilizes metal hand instruments using only dry ultraviolet light between patients.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the surface detail of a dental stone cast if air bubbles remain trapped in the mix?
Why should a Scout add dental stone powder slowly to measured water rather than pouring water onto powder?
Which dietary pattern in a three-day food log creates more acid attacks: one dessert at dinner or sipping soda?
What role does the mechanical dental vibrator play while pouring mixed stone into an alginate impression?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Topical fluoride in toothpaste and varnish continually remineralizes early enamel lesions and forms acid-resistant fluorapatite.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Fluoride only protects developing teeth in children and provides no benefit to adult tooth enamel.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Saliva contains amylase to initiate starch digestion, bicarbonate ions to buffer acids, and minerals to repair tooth enamel.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Saliva serves only to moisten food for swallowing and plays no chemical role in digesting nutrients.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Oral bacteria and inflammatory mediators from periodontal disease can enter the bloodstream and worsen systemic health conditions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Chronic gum inflammation stays confined to the mouth and cannot affect cardiovascular or systemic health.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Spitting out excess foam without rinsing leaves a concentrated fluoride film on enamel to aid repair while you sleep.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rinsing vigorously with water immediately after night brushing helps fluoride penetrate deeper into teeth.

extra_socratic_questions: What chemical change occurs when fluoride ions replace hydroxyl groups in tooth enamel crystal lattices?
Which salivary enzyme begins breaking down complex dietary starches before food ever reaches the stomach?
Under what condition does systemic fluoride intake during early childhood cause dental fluorosis in enamel?
What happens to oral pH and cavity risk when medications or dehydration severely reduce saliva flow?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hard bristles and aggressive sawing motions wear away root cementum and cause gum recession; use soft bristles at 45 degrees.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hard-bristled toothbrushes and heavy horizontal scrubbing clean plaque off teeth better than soft bristles.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Floss should be curved into a C-shape against one tooth surface and glided gently up and down just beneath the gum margin.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sawing floss back and forth across the bottom of the gum triangle is the proper way to clean between teeth.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only products that submit laboratory and clinical data proving safety and efficacy earn the voluntary ADA Seal of Acceptance.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every commercial toothpaste sold in stores carries the American Dental Association Seal of Acceptance.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Whitening agents and silica abrasives remove surface stains, whereas active fluoride ions are what protect enamel from decay.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Whitening toothpastes prevent cavities better than standard fluoridated pastes because they contain abrasives.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a Scout angle the toothbrush bristles along the gumline to demonstrate the modified Bass method?
Why is it dangerous to snap dental floss straight down onto the interdental papilla without curving it?
Which independent seal on a toothpaste package verifies that safety and decay-prevention claims were tested?
What motion should string follow against each side of a model tooth to remove interproximal plaque film?

extra_misconceptions.fact: DDS and DMD degrees have identical four-year curricula and clinical licensing standards; only the university Latin title differs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Doctor of Dental Surgery degree requires more years of dental school than a Doctor of Medicine in Dentistry.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dental hygienists complete accredited degree programs and pass board exams to perform periodontal scaling, unlike assistants.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dental hygienists and chairside dental assistants hold the same state license and scope of clinical practice.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Graduates must pass the Integrated National Board Dental Examination, a clinical board exam, and state jurisprudence licensing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Graduating from dental school automatically authorizes a dentist to practice in any state without exams.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Recognized dental specialties require two to six years of full-time accredited hospital or university residency after dental school.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dental specialties like endodontics or periodontics require only a weekend continuing education certificate.

extra_socratic_questions: What clinical procedures can a licensed dental hygienist perform independently that a dental assistant cannot?
Which standardized admission exam and undergraduate science prerequisites are required for dental school?
What post-doctoral residency training separates an orthodontist or oral surgeon from a general dentist?
Why must a dental laboratory technician understand bite biomechanics without treating patients directly?
